title: Experiment: totals against an oracle, and a corrupted artifact reported and recovered live
summary: Two measurements. OFFLINE, against a fixture whose composition was declared in the test — three requirements, two assertions, one decision — the counting rule returned exactly that; corrupting one requirement returned two requirements with every other type unchanged, and left the bad file visible with a parse error carrying a line and column. IN PRODUCTION, against a copy of `planning-content` served by a real build: the displayed assertion total equalled the number of parsable assertion files counted independently outside the application; corrupting one file with the server running dropped that total by exactly one, left every other type unchanged, rendered `data-vpw-unreadable-at="planning-content/data/assertions/…json:1:3"`, and kept the stages and lint regions rendered; restoring the file returned the total and cleared the error state, all without a rebuild or a restart.

facts.contentRoot: a disposable copy; the project's own content was not touched

omissions.reason: Only invalid JSON was exercised. A file that is unreadable for another reason — permissions, a directory in place of a file, an encoding fault — reaches the same code path but was not tested, and would report whatever message the read threw rather than a line and column.
One corrupt file at a time. The panel renders a list and the count is per type, so several should behave the same way, but that is reasoning rather than measurement.

The lint region was asserted to still RENDER while a file was corrupt, not that its findings are correct in that state. What the lint reports about a project with an unparsable artifact is the lint's business and is surfaced unchanged (#47).

notes: ⚠️ THE ORACLE IS WHAT MAKES THIS A TEST. The original ACC-0014 asked that each displayed total equal 'the number rendered on the page' — and the page renders TOTALS, not entries, so it compared a number with itself and would have passed on an implementation printing a constant. Both halves here count parsable files independently of the application. ⚠️ FALSIFIED THE TWO WAYS THAT MATTER. A constant total fails the oracle comparison and the decrement assertion; suppressing the unreadable region fails the located-error assertion — and each fails only its own, which is what stops one check standing in for the other. ⚠️ A SECOND INSTANCE OF AST-0035 WAS FIXED HERE, in this project's own reader rather than in the skeleton: `artifactCount` was `lint.records.length`, which counts FILES including ones that failed to parse. It now counts documents. The defect had been sitting in the reader since TSK-0005 and had never been displayed.
